description: This course introduces the internal organization of modern computer systems. Students learn digital system fundamentals, processor organization, instruction execution, control unit design, memory hierarchy, input-output systems, pipelining and computer architecture concepts required for efficient computer system design.

syllabus.title: Introduction
syllabus.body: Introduction to digital electronics, combinational circuits, sequential circuits, basic machine principles, computer organization, representation of real-world data, machine-level programming concepts, subroutines, branching and macro facilities.

syllabus.title: Processor Design
syllabus.body: Processor organization, information representation, number systems, instruction cycle, instruction formats, addressing modes, arithmetic operations, fixed-point addition, subtraction, multiplication and division, ALU design, parallel processing, performance considerations and pipeline processors.

syllabus.title: Control Design
syllabus.body: Instruction sequencing and interpretation, hardwired control unit design, microprogrammed control, control memory organization and execution of microinstructions.

syllabus.title: Memory Organization
syllabus.body: Memory device characteristics, random access memory, serial access memory, virtual memory, memory hierarchy, page replacement policies, segmentation, paging, cache memory, associative memory and file organization.

syllabus.title: System Organization
syllabus.body: Programmed I/O, Direct Memory Access (DMA), interrupts, I/O processors, CPU-I/O interaction and system-level organization of computer systems.

outcomes: Understand the fundamentals of digital electronics, machine organization and data representation.
Analyze processor organization, instruction execution, ALU design and pipelined processors.
Design and evaluate hardwired and microprogrammed control units.
Understand memory hierarchy, virtual memory, cache organization and storage management techniques.
Analyze input-output organization, DMA, interrupts and complete computer system architecture.
